newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorean president calls for efforts to cut deficit.
newsitem.headline: SKorean president calls for efforts to cut deficit.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Monday told his cabinet ministers to make efforts to reduce the nation's current account deficit for calendar 1997 to half of this year's level, an official of the presidential Blue House said.

"The government is urged to take steps to reduce next year's current account deficit to half of this year's level through thrift and saving efforts and improvement of competitiveness," the official quoted Kim as saying.
The government projects this year's current account deficit will be about $20 billion, compared with an $8.9 billion shortfall in calendar 1995.
South Korea has said it would put its top policy priority on enhancing corporate competitiveness, which has been suffering from high business costs and low management efficiency.
